lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A tornado is coming, and you have about ten minutes. Here's how to build a shelter that can survive it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: First, go underground. Tornado winds rip things off the surface, but the ground below protects you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then you need walls that won't break. So you pour thick concrete, with steel bars inside.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Because in a tornado, the real danger is flying debris. A plank of wood can hit at over a hundred and sixty kilometers per hour.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But strong winds can also lift things up. So you anchor the shelter deep into the ground with steel rods.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The door is the weakest point. So you use a heavy steel door with three locking bolts.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Once you're inside, you still need air. So you add small vents with caps that keep debris out.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And you might be in there for hours. So you store water, a flashlight, a first aid kit and a radio.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the tornado hits, with winds over three hundred kilometers per hour. Above ground, almost nothing is safe.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But underground, your family is safe.
